why_not_step_2: RTDBSCAN and RayJoin proved structural runner execution but did not produce material Set-A gains; therefore Barnes-Hut is a replacement attempt to satisfy Step 1's material-exit requirement, not Step 2 generalization.

pre_audit_decision.reason: Do not spend pod time until the existing generic fused partner is routed through prepared_execution_session_runner as a productized runtime node.
pre_audit_decision.next_engine_action: Add an app-agnostic prepared-execution helper for aggregate-tree fused weighted-vector continuation and wire Barnes-Hut to it as an adapter.

required_comparisons_after_implementatio.historical_no_go_reference: productized runner-wrapped fused partner versus current prepared OptiX frontier-emission no-go / V2.x-style frontier route
required_comparisons_after_implementatio.primary_parity_control: productized runner-wrapped fused partner versus existing app-front-door fused Numba CUDA partner
required_comparisons_after_implementatio.control_interpretation: A V3 material claim may use the productized path against the old frontier/CPU baseline, but must not claim the runner wrapper itself is faster than the already-fused partner unless the parity control actually shows it.

parity_failure_rule.failure_action: If the productized runner is more than 5% slower than the existing app-front-door fused partner at any serious size, the pod packet is no-go for claim use and a runner overhead bug must be logged before promotion.

expected_effect.why_it_can_be_material: The fused partner avoids aggregate-frontier row emission, host frontier materialization, and host contribution materialization that dominate the old frontier-emission shape.
expected_effect.why_runner_wrapper_alone_may_not_be_mate: The existing app-front-door fused partner already removed those costs, so the runner must preserve its performance rather than pretend to create it.

goal_level_decision_audit.decision: Continue with Barnes-Hut as a Step 1 replacement material-probe candidate only after productizing the fused partner as a runtime-trunk node, not by running another app-front-door pod benchmark first.
goal_level_decision_audit.was_i_foolish: No after amendment. The audit no longer pretends Step 1 is complete and separates a real performance source from a runner-wrapper parity control.
goal_level_decision_audit.foolish_actions: The foolish action would be to compare against the slow OptiX frontier route only, hide that the fast fused partner already exists, and call that a pure runner win.
goal_level_decision_audit.other_path: Run pod immediately against the old OptiX route. That would likely produce a large number but would not prove the productized runtime path exists.
goal_level_decision_audit.different_path_now: First wire the generic fused partner through prepared_execution_session_runner; then run pod with both the historical no-go reference and the primary parity control.
